content: 1. The book Health Literacy: A Prescription to End Confusion, edited by Nielsen-Bohlman L, Panzer AM, and Kindig DA, was published by the National Academies Press in Washington, DC, in 2004. It provides a comprehensive exploration of health literacy and its implications for public health. 2. Nutbeam D. discussed the evolving concept of health literacy in his article published in Social Science and Medicine in 2008 (Volume 67, Issue 12, Pages 2072-2078). This work highlights the dynamic nature of health literacy and its role in health outcomes. 3. Von Wagner C and colleagues reviewed the relationship between health literacy and health actions, presenting a framework from the perspective of health psychology. Their findings were published in Health Education and Behavior in 2009 (Volume 36, Issue 5, Pages 860-877). 4. Aagaard-Hansen J, Mwanga JR, and Bruun B. examined social science perspectives on schistosomiasis control in Africa, analyzing past trends and future directions. Their work appeared in Parasitology in 2009 (Volume 136, Issue 13, Pages 1747-1758). 5. Nutbeam D. emphasized health literacy as a public health goal and discussed the challenges it poses for contemporary health education and communication strategies in the 21st century. This article was published in Health Promotion International in 2000 (Volume 15, Issue 3, Pages 259-267). 6. The WHO Technical Report Series No. 971 (2012) outlines research priorities for zoonoses and marginalized infections, as reported by the TDR Disease Reference Group. 7. Studies conducted in Mali and Senegal provided the first evidence of the feasibility of eliminating onchocerciasis using ivermectin treatment in endemic areas. These findings were published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2009 (Volume 3, Issue 7, Article e497). 8. Umur S. investigated the prevalence and economic significance of cystic echinococcosis in slaughtered ruminants in Burdur, Turkey. The results were published in the Journal of Veterinary Medicine, Infectious Diseases, and Veterinary Public Health in 2003 (Volume 50, Issue 5, Pages 247-252). 9. Zinsstag J and colleagues analyzed the transmission dynamics and economics of rabies control in dogs and humans in an African city. Their study was published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America in 2009 (Volume 106, Issue 35, Pages 14996-15001). 10. Rupprecht CE and colleagues explored the question of whether rabies can be eradicated in their article published in Developmental Biology in 2008 (Volume 131, Pages 95-121). 11. Mallewa M and colleagues reported on cases of rabies encephalitis in a malaria-endemic area in Malawi, Africa. Their findings were published in Emerging Infectious Diseases in 2007 (Volume 13, Issue 1, Pages 136-139). 12. Rupprecht CE, Hanlon CA, and Hemachudha T. revisited the topic of rabies in their article published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2002 (Volume 2, Issue 6, Pages 327-343). 13. Lembo T and colleagues evaluated a direct, rapid immunohistochemical test for rabies diagnosis. Their study appeared in Emerging Infectious Diseases in 2006 (Volume 12, Issue 2, Pages 310-313). 14. Kang B and colleagues assessed the performance of a rapid immunodiagnostic test kit for rabies virus. Their findings were published in the Journal of Virological Methods in 2007 (Volume 145, Issue 1, Pages 30-36). 15. Nishizono A and colleagues developed a simple and rapid immunochromatographic test kit for rabies diagnosis. Their work was published in Microbiology and Immunology in 2008 (Volume 52, Issue 4, Pages 243-249). 16. Markotter W and colleagues evaluated a rapid immunodiagnostic test kit for detecting African lyssaviruses in brain material. Their study was published in the Journal of Veterinary Research in 2009 (Volume 76, Pages 257-262). 17. Muller T and colleagues developed a mouse monoclonal antibody cocktail for post-exposure rabies prophylaxis in humans. Their findings were published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2009 (Volume 3, Issue 11, Article 542). 18. The WHO and Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation consultation on human and dog rabies prevention and control was held in Annecy, France, from October 7-9, 2009. The report was published by the World Health Organization in 2010. 19. Kunda J. conducted an epidemiological study on zoonoses in the context of brucellosis in Tanzania. This research was presented as a thesis at the University of Edinburgh in 2006. 20. Cadmus SI and colleagues reported on the presence of Mycobacterium bovis and M. tuberculosis in goats in Nigeria. Their findings were published in Emerging Infectious Diseases in 2009 (Volume 15, Issue 12, Pages 2066-2067). 21. The WHO Technical Report Series No. 971 (2012) includes an appendix listing the membership of the Disease-Specific Reference Group on Zoonoses and Marginalized Infectious Diseases of Poverty (DRG 6), detailing the expertise and affiliations of its members. 22. The report also provides an overview of disease-specific and thematic reference groups (DRGs/TRGs) hosted by various WHO country offices and institutions worldwide, focusing on infectious diseases of poverty. 23. The appendices include a detailed list of think tank members, their affiliations, and their contributions to global health research, including experts in parasitology, epidemiology, microbiology, and public health from institutions across the globe.
